to certain specified types of “Covered Businesses,” including “perfume stores,” in a
“Covered Geographic Area” that encompassed A&S’s Fine Fragrance location at 501
East Olympic Boulevard.13

course of its trade or business, received currency in excess of $3,000 in one transaction
or two or more related transactions in a 24-hour period, to report such transactions
electronically to FinCEN.14 The Los Angeles Fashion District GTO was effective from
October 9, 2014 through April 6, 2015.

statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 5324?
statutory.answer: Insufficient facts to determine whether 31 U.S.C. § 5324 applies; § 5324 prohibits structuring only when done for the purpose of evading a reporting requirement, and the fact pattern does not show intent or any transactions near the $10,000 CTR threshold.
statutory.label: neutral
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5324 prohibits structuring (or attempting to structure) transactions with a domestic financial institution for the purpose of evading the reporting requirements of 31 U.S.C. § 5313(a) (CTR reporting generally triggered by currency transactions over $10,000 in a single day). Element-by-element: (1) Covered transactions with a domestic financial institution: the facts show multiple cash ATM withdrawals at U.S. branches and one wire transfer, so there are transactions involving a financial institution, but § 5324 is aimed at evasion of currency-transaction reporting. (2) Structuring/attempting to structure: the listed cash withdrawals are small (roughly $215–$731 each) and spread across dates/locations; there is no indication of breaking up a larger cash transaction into multiple transactions to avoid a reportable amount. (3) Purpose to evade reporting: the statute requires intent—i.e., that the transactions were conducted ‘for the purpose of evading’ CTR reporting under § 5313(a). The fact pattern provides no evidence of intent (e.g., statements, instructions to avoid reporting, pattern of same-day cash transactions totaling just under $10,000, or other indicia). (4) Reporting threshold nexus: none of the cash transactions are near $10,000, and there is no same-day aggregation approaching the CTR threshold, making it unclear that any reporting requirement was implicated. Therefore, based on the provided facts, it cannot be determined that § 5324 prohibits structuring in this scenario.
